points.text: CommonGen metric differences are tiny (second or third decimal).
Results lack seeds, variance, or significance tests.
Some variants are worse than the standard HMM on several metrics.
Claims of significant quality gains and halved max perplexity overstated; max perplexity is an outlier statistic.
Constraint satisfaction claim not measured since Ctrl-G satisfies constraints by construction.
VLM experiment small, single configuration, missing CIs and setup details.
Fluency preservation overstated; perplexity rises about 50% over vanilla.
Monte Carlo baseline capped at one sample is a strawman.
Missing standard controlled-decoding baselines like FUDGE or GeDi.
No ablation showing visual context is what helps the HMM.
Hateful Memes with Perspective API is a weak, noisy testbed.
Distillation results only in figures; headline gains unquantified, no base LM reference.
Comparison to Lee and Berg-Kirkpatrick dismissed without data.
Gains concentrate on first tokens, limiting benefit for distant-future constraints.
Minimal inference overhead claim not measured; no wall-clock or memory numbers.
Fine-tuned backbone variant contradicts fixed base LM pitch; deployment unclear.
Modest extension of Ctrl-G/TRACE; no comparison to hybrid neural-tractable models.
Proposition 1 is a trivial standard bound and inconsistently numbered.
No analysis of expressiveness lost by fixed transition and emission parameters.
Only GPT-2-large and a 2B VLM; no modern larger LMs.
Only one CommonGen Ctrl-G setting and no text TRACE experiment or RealToxicityPrompts comparison.
Presentation inconsistencies: model names, variant names, typos, duplicated reference.
Related work and conclusion merged and very short.
Datasets, training budgets, hidden sizes, encoder training details absent from main text.
Experimental setup details (learning rate, batch size) for neural HMM insufficient.
No generated sample examples, e.g. for detoxification.
Only two downstream tasks; other controlled-generation tasks not evaluated.
Baselines too limited; prior controlled generation algorithms not compared.
A visual diagram of the method would aid understanding.
Lookahead effectiveness diminishes for longer continuations due to limited latent capacity.
Simple HMM structure limits expressiveness, hindering practical generation use.
Lookup table becomes very large with large C and latent size.
Only GPT-2 and Qwen2-VL; newer or larger LLMs not tested.
Only short sequences up to 32 tokens; longer contexts not tested.
Only marginal perplexity gains over standard HMMs.
Fluency gains do not align with BLEU or ROUGE; discrepancy unexplained.
Missing controllable-generation baselines like FUDGE and GeDi.
Experiments mainly on medium-sized models; stronger LLMs needed.
Constraints synthetic or benchmark-style; real-world control settings untested.
Efficiency in streaming or large-batch inference and memory footprint unclear.
Theory (MI bound) not linked to empirical metrics or design choices.
Ablation of architectural choices limited, e.g. Monarch gains and encoder-HMM trade-off.
Limitations and failure cases not analysed.
Framing covers tractable models broadly but only HMM evaluated.
Figure 1 example not explained and no takeaway drawn.
Related work and conclusion blended; positioning relative to prior work unclear.
Missing Sequential Monte Carlo baseline.
More datasets needed to assess robustness and generality.
No evaluation on long contexts.
Lacks benchmarks against established controllable generation methods.
Appendix C lacks computational trade-off analysis.
